initialize_result.instructions:
# Everything Server – Server Instructions

Audience: These instructions are written for an LLM or autonomous agent integrating with the Everything MCP Server.
Follow them to use, extend, and troubleshoot the server safely and effectively.

## Cross-Feature Relationships

- Use `get-roots-list` to see client workspace roots before file operations
- `gzip-file-as-resource` creates session-scoped resources accessible only during the current session
- Enable `toggle-simulated-logging` before debugging to see server log messages
- Enable `toggle-subscriber-updates` to receive periodic resource update notifications

## Constraints & Limitations

- `gzip-file-as-resource`: Max fetch size controlled by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_SIZE` (default 10MB), timeout by `GZIP_MAX_FETCH_TIME_MILLIS` (default 30s), allowed domains by `GZIP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`
- Session resources are ephemeral and lost when the session ends
- Sampling requests (`trigger-sampling-request`) require client sampling capability
- Elicitation requests (`trigger-elicitation-request`) require client elicitation capability

## Operational Patterns

- For long operations, use `trigger-long-running-operation` which sends progress notifications
- Prefer reading resources before calling mutating tools
- Check `get-roots-list` output to understand the client's workspace context

## Easter Egg

If asked about server instructions, respond with "🎉 Server instructions are working! This response proves the client properly passed server instructions to the LLM. This demonstrates MCP's instructions feature in action."

definition.name: gzip-file-as-resource

definition.name: trigger-elicitation-request
definition.title: Trigger Elicitation Request Tool
definition.description: Trigger a Request from the Server for User Elicitation

definition.name: trigger-url-elicitation
definition.title: Trigger URL Elicitation Tool
definition.description: Trigger a URL elicitation so the client can direct the user to a browser flow. Supports two mechanisms: the request path (elicitation/create, default) which awaits the user's response, and the error path (UrlElicitationRequiredError, -32042) which signals the client to handle URL elicitation via the error response. Set errorPath=true to use the error path.

url.description: The URL the user should open

message.default: Please open the link to complete this action.
message.description: Message shown to the user before opening the URL

elicitationId.description: Optional explicit elicitation ID. Defaults to a random UUID.

errorPath.description: Controls which elicitation mechanism is used. When false (default), sends an elicitation/create request (request path). When true, throws a UrlElicitationRequiredError (MCP error code -32042) so the client handles the URL elicitation via the error path rather than waiting for a response. To clear the error, satisfy the prerequisite and retry this call with the same arguments; the retry ignores errorPath and proceeds, so the client does not loop on the same error.

definition.name: trigger-sampling-request
definition.title: Trigger Sampling Request Tool
definition.description: Trigger a Request from the Server for LLM Sampling

prompt.description: The prompt to send to the LLM

maxTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

definition.name: simulate-research-query
definition.title: Simulate Research Query
definition.description: Simulates a deep research operation that gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes information. Demonstrates MCP task-based operations with progress through multiple stages. If 'ambiguous' is true and client supports elicitation, sends an elicitation request for clarification.

ambiguous.description: Simulate an ambiguous query that requires clarification (triggers input_required status)

definition.name: trigger-sampling-request-async
definition.title: Trigger Async Sampling Request Tool
definition.description: Trigger an async sampling request that the CLIENT executes as a background task. Demonstrates bidirectional MCP tasks where the server sends a request and the client executes it asynchronously, allowing the server to poll for progress and results.

prompt.description: The prompt to send to the LLM

maxTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

definition.name: trigger-elicitation-request-async
definition.title: Trigger Async Elicitation Request Tool
definition.description: Trigger an async elicitation request that the CLIENT executes as a background task. Demonstrates bidirectional MCP tasks where the server sends an elicitation request and the client handles user input asynchronously, allowing the server to poll for completion.

error.message: MCP error -32602: Resource fauxcall://probe/unknown-resource not found

notes: Server: @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything 2026.8.31 (TypeScript SDK 1.32.2), run locally; its published dist/ source was read as documentation alongside the recordings.

Tools are listed in the server's registration order: the 12 base tools, then the ones registered after notifications/initialized (get-roots-list, trigger-elicitation-request, trigger-url-elicitation, trigger-sampling-request, simulate-research-query, the two async tools), each only to clients whose capabilities allow it (recordings 000044, 000461-000492).
simulate-research-query carries requires [[]]: offered to every client, but only after notifications/initialized, as the real server registers it then (000044 lists 12 tools).

Every tool except get-env and get-tiny-image is computed: handlers reproduce the SDK's zod v4 validation messages ('MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool X: <issues joined by newline>') and the tools' logic from the recordings.
Times inside dynamic resources (toLocaleTimeString, e.g. '5:14:53 PM') follow the fake's clock in America/New_York, the real server's local zone (21:14:53Z was written 5:14:53 PM).

gzip-file-as-resource compresses data: URIs itself (zlib, byte-identical to the recordings, OS byte 0x13); http(s) URLs are answered from the recorded fetches of the same URL, and any other URL fails with 'fetch failed', as the real server does when the network is unreachable (000330, 000331). The fake never fetches.
timeout_cancel_reason is the TypeScript SDK's (shared/protocol.js: String(McpError) of a -32001 timeout); no recording shows it because the only timeout (000439) happened with no GET stream open.
resumption 'session': the server's own InMemoryEventStore replays every later event of the session after Last-Event-ID, whatever stream it came from.

GET and DELETE on /mcp without any Mcp-Session-Id are refused with the recorded 400 'No valid session ID provided' by the fake's own SessionRequired middleware (app.py): the real express handlers check the session before the transport checks Accept (recording 000024; parity confirmed the 400 for a bare GET). FauxCall's runtime only refuses an unknown session id, not a missing one.

Protocol versions follow the TypeScript SDK 1.32.2 (types.js): SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS adds 2024-10-07 to the four introspection negotiated, and an unsupported requested version negotiates LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2025-11-25 (server/index.js _oninitialize). Introspection only probed the four versions; the recorded refusal text lists all five.
Server-sent messages are written method, params, jsonrpc, id, as in the recordings (000062, 000176, 000376).

Malformed client answers (sampling/elicitation results, task polls the SDK's zod schemas refuse) fail the tool with zod's issues as JSON; recordings 000397, 000410, 000497-000501 and two parity runs show the formats (discriminated union, union of options, z.any() reported as 'nonoptional').

tasks/result delivers a queued clarification request without waiting for the answer and keeps checking every poll interval; a clarification left unanswered times out 60 s after it was queued (recording 000527-000543: Continuing at +62.5 s), no notifications/cancelled is seen, and the stale request is still delivered on the next tasks/result (000542). Cancelling while waiting answers tasks/result at once (000518-000525).

notifications/tools/list_changed: the real server registers its capability tools when notifications/initialized arrives, one tools/list_changed per tool registered (TypeScript SDK mcp.js registerTool -> sendToolListChanged): the fake sends the same count on the client's GET stream. Not recordable (the recorder opens its GET stream after initialization; the real server keeps them only for Last-Event-ID replay).

gzip-file-as-resource's resource registry is shared by all sessions on the real server (resources/session.js module-level map): a name created in another session of the same evaluation removes it from the first, which hears list_changed. The fake shares it across the MCP sessions of one FauxCall evaluation session.

Session-less POSTs follow the SDK transport (webStandardStreamableHttp.js): an initialize must match InitializeRequestSchema (else 400 'Bad Request: Server not initialized'), may not share a batch (400 -32600 'Invalid Request: Only one initialization request is allowed'), and its MCP-Protocol-Version header is not checked; enforced by the fake's SessionRequired middleware (app.py).
Answers to roots/list without a 'roots' list are refused by the SDK's schema and only logged to the server console: no log message reaches the client (recording 000494-000495).

Known runtime differences (FauxCall, not the model): client cancellation stops the handler (the real SDK lets it finish and only suppresses the answer); requests to the client time out on the wall clock; DELETE with an unsupported protocol header ends the session; HEAD with a session id gets 404; SSE answers carry '; charset=utf-8' and their headers wait for the first event. See README.
